key_concepts: Plants reproduce to sustain their species
Some plants reproduce by seeds while others use vegetative parts
The stamen is the male reproductive organ of a flower
The pistil is the female reproductive organ of a flower
The pistil has stigma, style, and ovary; the ovary contains ovules
The stamen has anther and filament; the anther contains pollen sacs
Runners are horizontal above-ground stems with buds that form new plants
Suckers are upright shoots from buds at the base of parent stems
Bulbs are underground stems with stored food and buds that produce new shoots
Rhizomes are underground or surface stems with nodes that can produce new plants
Tubers are swollen modified roots that can grow new plants
Plantlets are small plants produced on leaf edges
